journeys.title: Who I am today
journeys.subtitle: OTT · identity, state, and description
journeys.learningGoal: Use ben, bent, is, and zijn for a present identity, state, or description.

story.nl: Ik ben vandaag rustig.
story.english: I am calm today.

story.nl: Ik ben thuis en ik ben klaar.
story.english: I am at home and I am ready.
story.telugu: నేను ఇంట్లో ఉన్నాను మరియు సిద్ధంగా ఉన్నాను.

story.nl: Ik ben blij met mijn nieuwe kamer.
story.english: I am happy with my new room.
story.telugu: నా కొత్త గది నాకు సంతోషంగా ఉంది.

story.nl: Vandaag ben ik hier.
story.english: Today I am here.

story.nl: Ik ben niet alleen; mijn vrienden zijn hier.
story.english: I am not alone; my friends are here.
story.telugu: నేను ఒంటరిగా లేను; నా స్నేహితులు ఇక్కడ ఉన్నారు.

notice.title: The present forms of zijn
notice.subtitle: The subject decides which present form belongs in the sentence.
notice.formula: ik ben · jij bent · hij/het is · wij zijn
notice.formulaNote: Learn this as a bounded present-tense contrast. This journey does not claim full unconstrained production.
notice.valuableContrast: Ben, bent, is, and zijn are all present forms of zijn. Choose the form from the subject: ik ben, jij bent, hij is, wij zijn.

journeys.title: Questions I ask
journeys.subtitle: OTT · questions and inversion
journeys.learningGoal: Recognise ben je?, is het?, and zijn we? in present-tense questions.

story.nl: Ben je vandaag thuis?
story.english: Are you at home today?

story.nl: Is het hier rustig?
story.english: Is it quiet here?

story.nl: Zijn we op tijd?
story.english: Are we on time?

story.nl: Ik vraag of ik klaar ben.
story.english: I ask whether I am ready.

story.nl: Ik wil weten of mijn vrienden hier zijn.
story.english: I want to know whether my friends are here.
story.telugu: నా స్నేహితులు ఇక్కడ ఉన్నారా అని నేను తెలుసుకోవాలనుకుంటున్నాను.

notice.title: Questions turn the order around
notice.subtitle: In a direct yes/no question, the finite form comes before the subject.

comparison.label: question
comparison.meaning: ben comes before je in the question

comparison.label: past contrast
comparison.meaning: was places the state in the past

comparison.label: experience contrast
comparison.meaning: ben geweest describes a completed experience

notice.formula: Ben je? · Is het? · Zijn we?
notice.formulaNote: The finite form moves before the subject in a direct question: Ben je thuis? The embedded question Ik vraag of ik klaar ben keeps ordinary clause order.
notice.valuableContrast: Ben je vandaag thuis? is a present direct question. Was je gisteren thuis? changes the time to the past, while ben je al thuis geweest? asks about a completed experience.

journeys.title: Where I was
journeys.subtitle: OVT · past states and locations
journeys.learningGoal: Use was and waren for a past state, identity, or location.

story.nl: Ik was gisteren rustig.
story.english: I was calm yesterday.

story.nl: Ik was de hele ochtend thuis.
story.english: I was at home all morning.

story.nl: Na de lunch was ik in de stad.
story.english: After lunch I was in the city.

story.nl: Mijn vrienden waren ook in de stad.
story.english: My friends were also in the city.

story.nl: Aan het einde waren we moe maar blij.
story.english: At the end we were tired but happy.

notice.title: Was and waren look back
notice.subtitle: The past forms describe a state or location from a past viewpoint.

comparison.label: present contrast
comparison.meaning: ben keeps the state in the present

notice.formula: ik was · jij was · hij was · wij waren
notice.formulaNote: Was is used with singular subjects in this bounded contrast; waren is used with wij and other plural subjects.
notice.valuableContrast: Ik was gisteren thuis looks back to yesterday. Ik ben vandaag thuis stays in the present, while wij waren uses the plural past form.

journeys.title: Places I have been
journeys.subtitle: VTT · past experience and being somewhere
journeys.learningGoal: Use ben geweest and is geweest to talk about a completed experience or being somewhere.

story.nl: Ik ben al eens in dit museum geweest.
story.english: I have been in this museum once before.
story.telugu: నేను ఇంతకుముందు ఈ మ్యూజియంలో ఒకసారి ఉన్నాను.

story.nl: Ik ben hier met mijn broer geweest.
story.english: I have been here with my brother.

story.nl: Ik ben vorige maand in Utrecht geweest.
story.english: I was in Utrecht last month.

story.nl: Ik ben daar al twee keer geweest.
story.english: I have been there twice already.

story.nl: Mijn broer is er nog nooit geweest.
story.english: My brother has never been there.

notice.title: Being somewhere as a completed experience
notice.subtitle: Ben geweest and is geweest connect a past experience to the present viewpoint.

comparison.label: experience
comparison.sentence: Ik ben al eens in dit museum geweest.

comparison.label: past state
comparison.sentence: Ik was gisteren in het museum.

comparison.label: present state
comparison.sentence: Ik ben nu in het museum.

notice.formula: ik ben geweest · hij is geweest
notice.formulaNote: With zijn, VTT uses the present auxiliary ben or is plus geweest. This journey keeps the focus on being or having been, not on auxiliary constructions for another verb.
notice.valuableContrast: Ik ben in het museum geweest reports an experience. Ik was gisteren in het museum describes a past situation, while Ik ben nu in het museum describes the current location.

journeys.title: Where I will be
journeys.subtitle: OTTT + OVTT · future and conditional
journeys.learningGoal: Distinguish an explicit future state from a conditional possibility.

story.nl: Morgen zal ik thuis zijn.
story.english: Tomorrow I will be at home.

story.nl: Als het regent, zou ik thuis zijn.
story.english: If it rains, I would be at home.

story.nl: Na de afspraak zal ik op kantoor zijn.
story.english: After the appointment I will be at the office.

story.nl: Als ik meer tijd had, zou ik langer hier zijn.
story.english: If I had more time, I would be here longer.
story.telugu: నాకు ఎక్కువ సమయం ఉంటే, నేను ఇక్కడ ఎక్కువసేపు ఉండేవాడిని.

story.nl: Volgende week zal ik in Amsterdam zijn.
story.english: Next week I will be in Amsterdam.

notice.title: Plans and possibilities
notice.subtitle: Zal zijn makes a future state explicit; zou zijn frames it as conditional.

comparison.label: conditional
comparison.sentence: Als het regent, zou ik thuis zijn.

comparison.label: everyday future
comparison.meaning: ordinary Dutch with a future time word

notice.formula: ik zal zijn · ik zou zijn
notice.formulaNote: Zal points forward explicitly. Zou presents the state as conditional or hypothetical; everyday Dutch can use OTT with a clear future time word.
notice.valuableContrast: Morgen zal ik thuis zijn states a future plan. Als het regent, zou ik thuis zijn depends on a condition, while Morgen ben ik thuis is a common everyday future.

journeys.title: Completed reference points
journeys.subtitle: VVT + VTTT + VVTT · advanced completion
journeys.learningGoal: Recognise completed being states viewed from a past, future, or hypothetical reference point.

story.nl: Voordat de trein kwam, was ik al op het station geweest.
story.english: Before the train came, I had already been at the station.
story.telugu: రైలు రాకముందు నేను ఇప్పటికే స్టేషన్‌లో ఉన్నాను.

story.nl: Voor het einde van de dag zal ik thuis geweest zijn.
story.english: By the end of the day, I will have been at home.
story.telugu: రోజు ముగిసేలోపు నేను ఇంట్లో ఉండి ఉంటాను.

story.nl: Als ik eerder vertrok, zou ik op tijd geweest zijn.
story.english: If I left earlier, I would have been on time.

story.nl: Ik was al in de zaal geweest voordat de film begon.
story.english: I had already been in the hall before the film started.
story.telugu: సినిమా ప్రారంభమయ్యే ముందు నేను ఇప్పటికే హాల్‌లో ఉన్నాను.

story.nl: Tegen de avond zal ik al twee uur op kantoor geweest zijn.
story.english: By evening, I will have been at the office for two hours.
story.telugu: సాయంత్రానికి నేను కార్యాలయంలో రెండు గంటలు ఉండి ఉంటాను.

notice.title: Completion from another viewpoint
notice.subtitle: The same state can be completed before a past, future, or hypothetical reference point.

comparison.label: earlier past
comparison.sentence: Ik was al op het station geweest voordat de trein kwam.

comparison.label: future reference
comparison.sentence: Voor het einde van de dag zal ik thuis geweest zijn.

comparison.label: hypothetical result
comparison.sentence: Ik zou op tijd geweest zijn als ik eerder vertrok.

notice.formula: was geweest · zal geweest zijn · zou geweest zijn
notice.formulaNote: These are reference forms for reading and careful comparison. They keep zijn as the main/copular verb and do not introduce zijn as an auxiliary for another lexical verb.
notice.valuableContrast: Was geweest looks back from a past point. Zal geweest zijn looks forward to completion, while zou geweest zijn describes a hypothetical completed state.
